This could bring a financial windfall, an unexpected expense, or simply a sobering realization about the way you relate to money and stability. Whatever comes up, Taurus energy prefers a steady game plan over an impulsive reaction, especially with Venus retrograde right now. Review what’s working, release what’s draining you,  and get honest about what you actually need in order to feel secure both financially and emotionally. The end of October wants you grounded in what’s real, not rushing toward what is next.

Taurus, this first full week of Scorpio Season may make relationships feel a lot more  consuming than usual. You could find yourself excavating every layer of a connection,  reading more deeply into someone’s behavior, or feeling more possessive, protective, or even slightly obsessive about where you stand with people who matter to you. Scorpio energy can make intimacy feel all-or-nothing, and because it sits opposite your sign, it may pull you out of your usual comfort zone by asking you to confront the emotional undercurrents you would normally rather stabilize than dissect. Let yourself notice what is being revealed without turning every feeling into a final conclusion.

Then your annual Taurus Full Moon arrives on October 26th and brings the focus decisively back to you. A milestone from the past six months may become clear, or you may reach an emotional breaking point that ends up being the breakthrough you needed. This lunation asks you to come back to your body, your needs, your pace, and your own sense of self — the relationship that ultimately sets the tone for every other one. Let yourself feel whatever comes up without immediately trying to move past it, then use that clarity to create a steadier inner and outer foundation so you can end October feeling more rooted in who you are.

Gemini, this first full week of Scorpio Season asks you to go deeper than the surface level version of wellness. Green smoothies, strength training, and a perfectly organized routine can only take you so far if your mind is exhausted or your inner dialogue is constantly tearing you down. Scorpio energy pushes you to look more honestly at the psychological habits underneath your daily life: the way you speak to yourself, the stress you normalize, and the parts of you that are still performing “fine” when something clearly needs attention. This is a powerful week to shed habits and mindsets that no longer match the person you are becoming, and to replace self criticism with a much more compassionate form of discipline.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th lands in your spirituality, solitude, and subconscious sector, which may pull you slightly out of your comfort zone. You’re usually happiest when there’s movement, conversation, and something new to think about, but this lunation asks you to slow down enough to face what has been lingering underneath the noise. Old memories, insecurities, or people from the past may resurface, and the release could be surprisingly physical or emotional. Turn your notifications off, spend more time alone, meditate, journal, sit under a tree, hug one if you feel like it… anything that helps you come back into your body and out of mental overdrive. If you give yourself that space, you could end October feeling dramatically lighter and much more ready to soar into November.

Cancer, this first full week of Scorpio Season can feel like your heart is turning the volume up on everything that makes you feel alive. Romance, creativity, pleasure, and inner-child healing all come into sharper focus, but Scorpio asks you to go beyond surface-level fun and notice where desire is tangled up with fear, control, or old emotional conditioning. You may feel more passionate, more magnetic, or more creatively obsessed, but also more aware of what still makes you hesitate to fully enjoy yourself. Let this week show you where joy has been carrying emotional baggage, and give yourself permission to want what you want without immediately interrogating it.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th lights up your friendship, community, and future-goals sector, helping you see which people and plans actually feel stable enough to grow with you. A friendship, collaboration, or long-term goal may reach a milestone, or you may realize that a certain social dynamic has run its course. Taurus energy helps you come back to what’s consistent and trustworthy rather than what’s simply exciting in the moment. By the end of the month, you may feel much clearer about who belongs in your next chapter and which dreams are worth building slowly.

Leo, this first full week of Scorpio Season turns your attention toward home, family,  and the emotional foundation underneath everything else. You may feel more protective  of your space, more sensitive to old family dynamics, or more aware of where you have been carrying tension privately while still showing up confidently in public. Scorpio energy can excavate memories, loyalties, and emotional patterns that shaped you long before you had language for them. The goal this week isn’t to fix your entire past; it’s to understand what still has influence over you and decide what deserves to come with you into your next chapter.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th lights up your career, reputation, and public-image sector, bringing a culmination around something you’ve been building over the past six months. Recognition, a professional milestone, a decision about your direction, or even a realization that a certain version of success no longer satisfies you could come to the surface. Taurus asks you to move from pressure into sustainability, so pay attention to what feels solid rather than what simply looks impressive. By month’s end, the balance between your private life and public ambitions may feel much clearer, and that clarity can help you build a version of success that actually feels good to live inside of.

Virgo, this first full week of Scorpio Season asks you to pay much closer attention to the stories running through your mind all day. Your communication, thinking, learning, and immediate environment are activated, but Scorpio wants more than surface-level  observations. You may become aware of a thought pattern you repeat when you feel insecure, a conversation you keep replaying, or a truth you have been editing because saying it plainly felt too vulnerable. This week is powerful for deeper mental cleanup:  questioning assumptions, naming what you actually feel, and shedding ways of thinking that keep you hyper-vigilant rather than genuinely prepared.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th illuminates your expansion, travel, education, publishing, and belief sector, helping you zoom out after so much inner analysis. A goal you’ve been working toward over the past six months may reach a milestone, or you may feel ready to make a more grounded decision about where you want to go next. Taurus energy encourages you to trust the path that feels steady and sustainable rather than chasing movement for movement’s sake. By the end of the month, you may realize that your perspective has changed enough to make a whole  new future feel possible.

Libra, this first full week of Scorpio Season pulls you into a deeper conversation with money, self-worth, and the kind of security you actually trust. You may become more aware of where you spend to self-soothe, where you undervalue your time, or where your sense of worth still rises and falls depending on someone else’s approval. Scorpio energy wants you to get underneath the number in the bank account and look at the emotional story attached to it. This is a powerful week to shed scarcity habits,  comparison, or financial choices that no longer reflect who you are becoming, especially with Venus retrograde encouraging you to reassess what feels truly valuable.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th illuminates your intimacy, shared resources, and transformation sector, bringing a deeper relationship or financial matter to a turning point. A debt, agreement, emotional bond, or trust issue may reach some kind of culmination, and the lesson is to stay grounded enough to see what is actually sustainable. Taurus wants clear terms, steadiness, and reciprocity, so this Full Moon may help you recognize where you are overextended or where support is finally becoming available. By the end of October, you may feel much clearer about what you are willing to share, what you need to protect, and what kind of merging actually feels safe.

Scorpio, this first full week of your birthday season can feel like your energy is finally returning to you. After weeks of retrograde reflection, emotional excavation, and questioning what you still want, the sun in your sign gives you permission to take up more space again. You may feel more magnetic, more certain of your instincts, and more willing to move toward the version of your life that feels deeply yours. This is a powerful reset point for identity, confidence, appearance, desire, and personal direction. Let yourself celebrate how much you have already shed. You are entering a  new solar chapter with more self-knowledge than you had a year ago, and that alone  changes the way you move through everything next.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th illuminates your partnership sector and may reveal who’s actually equipped to soar with you into this next chapter. A relationship, friendship, collaboration, or commitment could reach an important milestone, while another may make it painfully obvious that loyalty has been keeping you attached past the expiration date. Scorpio can be loyal to a fault once someone has earned a place in your heart, but this Full Moon asks whether the connection is still reciprocal, grounded, and capable of growing with you. Let people reveal who they are. The right ones will not require you to shrink your evolution in order to keep them close.

Sag, this first full week of Scorpio Season may feel quieter than your usual rhythm, but there is a lot happening beneath the surface. Your solitude, subconscious, and healing zone is activated, so you may crave more privacy, more sleep, or simply more distance from people and situations that keep you mentally overstimulated. Scorpio Season can bring old emotions, fears, or unfinished chapters back into awareness, but the point is not to get lost in them. It is to understand what is draining your energy and what you are finally ready to release before your own season begins next month.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th lights up your work, wellness, and daily routine sector, helping you turn that inner awareness into something practical. A habit, responsibility, health matter, or work situation may reach a culmination, or you may realize your body has been trying to tell you something for a while. Taurus energy wants consistency over extremes, so resist the urge to overhaul your entire life overnight. One steady change to your schedule, boundaries, or self-care could do more for you than another burst of motivation that disappears by next week.

Capricorn, this first full week of Scorpio Season puts your attention on the people,  communities, and future plans that actually have enough substance to grow with you. You may feel more selective socially, more protective of your long-term vision, or more aware of which friendships inspire you versus which ones leave you depleted. Scorpio Season can deepen your sense of loyalty, but it can also make you question whether certain alliances are rooted in genuine support or simply history. This is a strong week to get serious about the kind of network you want around the life you are building next.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th lights up your romance, creativity, pleasure, and inner-child sector, bringing a much more personal kind of culmination. A love story, creative project, passion, or desire may reach an important milestone, and you may suddenly see how much joy you have been postponing in the name of responsibility. Taurus wants something you can actually feel and enjoy, so let this Full Moon reconnect you with what makes life worth all the effort. By the end of October, you may realize that pleasure deserves a permanent place in your plans, not just whatever time is left over.

Aquarius, this first full week of Scorpio Season puts real weight behind your ambitions and the way you want to be known. Your career, reputation, and public image are activated, but Scorpio energy makes this more than a simple productivity push. You may feel more strategic, more selective about what you attach your name to, and more aware of where you have been chasing visibility without enough emotional investment behind it. This is a strong week to deepen your commitment to the work that actually matters to you and to move with intention rather than trying to prove yourself everywhere at once.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th pulls you back toward home, family, and your emotional foundation. A living situation, family matter, or private emotional need may reach a turning point, and you could suddenly realize that external success feels very different when your inner world is unsettled. Taurus energy asks you to stabilize from the inside out. Give yourself permission to slow down, protect your space, and define what security looks like beyond achievement. That grounding can help you end  October feeling much more centered about where you are going next.

Pisces, this first full week of Scorpio Season can make you hungry for meaning in a way that feels almost impossible to ignore. Your expansion, travel, education, publishing, spirituality, and belief sector is activated, so you may find yourself questioning whether the life you’re living is still big enough for the person you are becoming. Scorpio adds emotional depth to those questions, which can make a certain dream, destination, field of study, or spiritual path feel more urgent than usual. Follow what keeps pulling at you, but let the retrograde atmosphere keep you reflective enough to understand why it matters before you make any sweeping decisions.

Then the Taurus Full Moon on October 26th lights up your communication, learning, and immediate-environment sector, helping you bring all of that bigger-picture thinking  back down to earth. A conversation, writing project, sibling dynamic, decision, or piece of news may reach a turning point and give language to something you have been sensing for weeks. Taurus wants clarity that can actually be used, so simplify what feels overly complicated and say what you mean. By the end of October, you may feel  much more grounded in your own voice and clearer about which ideas are worth carrying forward.

items.title: The Full Hunter’s Moon In Taurus Will Make You Thirsty For Extra Attention
items.description: On October 26th, right after midnight on the eastern border, the Full Moon in Taurus appears. October's Hunter’s Moon (also known as the Travel or Falling Leaves Moon) brightly illuminates the sky, revealing all that is hidden. With Samhain and Halloween less
items.author: Lisa Stardust
paragraphs: On October 26th, right after midnight on the eastern border, the Full Moon in Taurus appears. October's Hunter’s Moon (also known as the Travel or Falling Leaves Moon) brightly illuminates the sky, revealing all that is hidden. With Samhain and Halloween less than a week after the lunation, this is an especially sensitive time; the veil between the physical and spiritual worlds is thin, offering moments of heightened intuition. The Hunter's Moon offers a chance to see in the dark as we shed our past and negative habits to work toward a better present and future.

Traditionally, the Hunter’s Moon is a time when people would forage for food and track their prey to ensure nourishment in the colder months of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. It is the middle of fall, urging us to work harder to provide for those we care about and wish to protect. This year, the Hunter’s Moon is in the sign of Taurus, exalting the lunar demand for security and indulgence. Not only do we want to build a strong foundation, but we also to have our cake and eat it, too. Nothing is too good for us, and we demand the best of the best. Why not? We deserve it!

The intensity of Pluto in Aquarius, forming a T-square with the sun in Scorpio and the moon in Taurus, isn't lost on us. The infamous Scorpio stingers may come out as a defense to safeguard our hearts. Hope for transformation and group growth exists if we are willing to access the higher vibration of these planets. However, most of us may not be able to be as levelheaded. When we feel as though others are attacking us right now, we may react fiercely and provocatively, striking back and asserting our feelings. The Scorpion's poisonous appendages may come out, causing us to use our words to hurt others. As much as we deflect our pain, it won't help, except for momentary vindication, which is why it's best to try to mend offenses and build a better dynamic instead.

Luckily, the moon in Taurus aims to give us a softer edge and a calmer approach, and to help us understand that the people in our lives are loyal; conversely, the caveat is that our stubbornness may cause us to dig our heels in the mud when we are pushed to the limit; we are going to scuffle and hustle. Still, the quarrel will be cathartic in the end; the Full Moon in Taurus doesn't want to end relationships, but enhance them. Keep that in mind before saying things we may regret. Do not take the drama to the extreme.

At this juncture, Venus (the planetary ruler of Taurus, the sign of the Full Moon) is retrograde in Libra (Venus backed up into the air sign on October 25th). Venus retrograde in Libra offers a combustible window of passion — our patience will be tested. The incessant need to partner with others puts pressure on both the other person and us. We might overlook their flaws to keep a commitment going, even though we criticize their behavior. Being kind and compassionate to our partners is essential if forging a relationship is on the horizon. We may also be thirsty for extra attention. There is nothing wrong with requiring affection.

Simultaneously, Mercury is moonwalking in Scorpio (the backslide officially began on October 24th). Revelations from the past will surface as the skeletons we buried deep in our consciousness come out. The reason is that Mercury retrograde in Scorpio is seeking to uncover the truth, and combined with the Full Moon, it offers an opportunity for us to tell those we are close to about our misfortune, insecurities, and emotional states, as we purge ourselves of what we felt was taboo in an effort to be understood.

Letting go of our old beliefs and invigorating our auras with newness isn’t something that comes easily. But we can shape and tend to who we are and what we value — and seek refuge in the tender arms of a friend, family member, or partner who supports us in these trying times.

items.title: The Gentle Horror of Kate Zambreno’s Foam
items.description: Inspired by the soft sculptures of Eva Hesse, the author’s experimental new novel, published by Semiotext(e), explores the demands of caregiving and work on artistic life
items.author: P Eldridge
paragraphs: Inspired by the soft sculptures of Eva Hesse, the author’s experimental new novel, published by Semiotext(e), explores the demands of caregiving and work on artistic life

There’s a distinct, lingering atmosphere that settles over the pages of Kate Zambreno’s new novel, Foam – a weight that feels at once ephemeral and suffocating. An experimental novel punctuated with doubles – a multiplying sequence of figures named “Eva” – Foam exists as a space of domestic cataloguing, art criticism and bodily fragmentation; an assemblage of residues, grief and routine. And beneath its sensory observations nestles a sharper, far more terrifying confrontation – “a gentle horror”, as Zambreno puts it: an examination of how contemporary creative existence is drained by capitalist institutions, and how, with the precarity of rental housing and caregiving, we inadvertently reconstruct those same frameworks within the walls of our own homes.

The American novelist, essayist and professor has long been a master of capturing the precarious position of the artist operating at the margins of academia and the gig economy. In Foam, the narrator is an adjunct writing professor without the luxury of maternity leave across two births – the latter depicted in a strange horror-filled pandemic delivery stripped of compassion. The pressure of unrelenting deadlines and classes to cover summer rent fuses institutional logic directly to the domestic walls. The modern machine demands metricised efficiency and a total monetisation of interiority. Creativity dissolves into administrative labour: emails, grants, and constant Zoom presence. Exhausted yet persistent, the narrator navigates these oppressive demands while trying to care for two young children.

The opening of Foam traces the narrator’s transition into postpartum caregiving and the presence of “The Evas” – writing students hired as in-home helpers and assistants for the narrator – but this is no bourgeois nursery memoir. Care is navigated in a rundown, shabby apartment amid landlord hostilities and lead paint. “The Evas” who occupy the first part of the novel are not traditional nannies but former students whose own ambitions, jealousies, and anxieties mirror the narrator’s desire for creative autonomy. Foam’s narrator experiences a profound collision between the gendered expectations of selfless devotion and the pressures of becoming a disembodied parental role model when trying to cover rent and survive. “I’ve had to reason with writing about the exploitation and extraction of adjuncting; to look at these episodes in my life that have brought me the most guilt,” Zambreno tells me over Zoom from their home in New York. “I honestly think there’s no truly ethical way to pay someone else to take care of your child.”

Foam’s scope then broadens into durational performance, material decay, art criticism, institutional violence, and physical breakdown. The narrative shifts in unconventional ways, functioning like the philosopher Peter Sloterdijk’s description of foam, which is the novel’s epigraph: “Almost nothing, yet not nothing. A something, if only a delicate web of cavities and subtle walls. An actual thing, but a construct fearful of contact that yields and bursts at the slightest touch.” The novel’s form physically transforms, as you read, into its title; fissures and soft structures that reject rigid demands or expectations.

This shift is not without an anchored, deep engagement with feminist art practices and soft sculptures. Zambreno weaves art criticism directly into the fiction, thinking through artist Eva Hesse’s latex and fibreglass works – Repetition 19 and Expanded Expansion – which degrade and rot over time. Hesse’s ethos becomes the intellectual spine: “Life doesn’t last: art doesn’t last” … “I have lost my fear of the ugly.” This obsession with ephemerality and non-form extends to Senga Nengudi’s RSVP – sculptures stretched and weighted by sandbags to reflect the “sagging form after pregnancy” – and Gabriela Salazar’s study of apartment windows that shows “the melancholy of apartment living. The walls become shabby, and only after the tenants disappear, so there’s no trace, do the walls get painted over, as if no one ever existed before,” as Zambreno writes. The name “Eva” rattles and echoes through the text, not merely as the former writing students, but as an expansive motif: the artist Eva Hesse, the cardiologist named Eva, a childhood doll, a friend’s child, a couple’s vibrator, and the mother of a previous lover – multiplying until the self becomes a soft sculpture in flux.

Through this scaffolding, Foam and its language become preoccupied with the body under extreme stress and pressure: postpartum haemorrhaging, repetitive nursing, high blood pressure, the “100-day cough” and a sudden fainting where the narrator collapses on a busy Brooklyn street while clutching a baby. The medical apparatus is no refuge either, delivering cold gaslighting where a cardiologist dismisses heart pain and trauma with automated advice.

Institutional cruelty occurs throughout Foam, as much in the domestic sphere as in the university. Zambreno charts the horror of student suicides – where neoliberal universities respond with hollow wellness initiatives like handing out polyurethane foam stress balls – and the Kafkaesque bureaucracy of middle managers. The novel insists that under capitalism, institutions will never love you; a reminder that you can’t escape the conditions of your own life, nor the conditions of governing institutions and how they hold power, class privilege, and control over you; and you, whatever your creed, might be inadvertently reconstructing facets of a politic you’re against in the most political of all places: your home. We’ve all heard the adage, ‘the personal is political’. Foam is the first novel worthy of that simple yet guttural language, having built an extraordinary, durational monument out of a “wildly interior book” that is fragile and absurd, carved from the residues of physical exhaustion.

Ultimately, Foam stays with the textures of the everyday. It pays exquisite attention to the fragile, useless, and unquantifiable moments of union that resist capitalist capture: the softness of a child’s sweater, the erratic drift of thought, the accumulation of clutter, the tactile sensation of foam itself, and the ephemerality of durational performance and sculpture. “Foam is maybe not the most transformational or optimistic work, but it’s shot through with that gentle horror of pessimism […] Nothing too bad happens, but there’s a bad feeling, alongside the moments of joy which act as a relief from capitalism,” says Zambreno. By centering these fleeting, mutable and anti-capitalist textures, Zambreno acknowledges that while we may never fully untangle our domestic lives from the institutional logic that feeds us, we can still cultivate moments of pleasure within the ruins of a mouldy home.

Zambreno achieves something profoundly tender by turning the very things capitalism dismisses as waste into a sacred liturgy. The brilliance of the novel is that it doesn’t offer any grand political escape route. You and I and Zambreno are stuck in something truer: a clear-eyed account of precarity, domestic captivity, bodily endurance and a delicate insistence on making art out of the very residue of our own enervation.
Foam is out now, published by Semiotext(e)

items.title: Twenty-One Conversations with Architects by Arquitectura-G
items.description: Twenty-One Conversations with Architects by Arquitectura-G has been added to your shopping bag
paragraphs: Twenty-One Conversations with Architects by Arquitectura-G has been added to your shopping bag

Twenty-One Conversations with Architects brings together more than a decade and a half’s worth of interviews conducted by Barcelona-based architecture firm Arquitectura-G, published in Apartamento magazine since its very first issue in 2008. Expansive, technical, submerged, the book threads together some of architecture’s most singular minds, crossing decades, archives, disciplines, and countries, and placing multiple generations of architects side by side in a single volume. What started as a takeover of the magazine’s architecture section has now become something else entirely: a portrait of the studio itself, their own obsessions surfacing across every conversation—questions of scale, ambiguity, hedonism, bathrooms, dances, the house as a laboratory. As they open these interviews to the anthology, the architects unfold a series of choices in houses and homes that are deeply personal to those who conceived them, united by their fundamental questioning of universal needs answered by universal forms. What ties these houses together is something beyond architecture—less about having built them, and more about having gone on living inside the questions they raised. Twenty-one conversations later, Arquitectura-G draws each architect into a new one—curated together, and compiled by Moisés Puente, they are now asked to speak to each other across time.

Arquitectura-G is a Barcelona-based architecture studio founded in 2006 by Jonathan Arnabat, Jordi Ayala-Bril, Igor Urdampilleta, and Aitor Fuentes. Their practice spans ephemeral installations, residential projects, retail, and urban planning, with work published widely in international media. In 2015 they received the prestigious 2015 Mies Van der Rohe Award for Emerging Architects. They also teach, returning to the school where they first met. Since 2008 they have edited the architecture section of Apartamento magazine, a collaboration that also traces the development of their critical thinking.
Published by Apartamento Publishing S.L.
Release date: September 16, 2026
Shipping method: DHL/UPS courier service with tracking
Delivery time: 2-4 days from the shipping confirmation

items.title: Kam Patterson Is Too Funny to Play It Safe
items.description: Top CALVIN KLEIN, shirt and pants MFPEN, shoes UGG
items.author: Jazmine Hughes
paragraphs: Top CALVIN KLEIN, shirt and pants MFPEN, shoes UGG

This past January, halfway through his first season as a Saturday Night Live cast member, Kam Patterson returned to his roots: a stand-up set on “Kill Tony.” The long-running live podcast is taped in Austin, Texas, an unlikely new hub of American comedy — a place where people pushed out of or fed up with New York or Los Angeles can strike new ground.

“Kill Tony” is one of the city’s premier showcases, averaging a few million downloads every episode. It’s where Patterson first started getting attention as a comic in 2023, so it made sense that he’d return with a piping-fresh report from the front lines of the East Coast.
Jacket and pants PUBLIC SCHOOL, top NOAH, shoes UGG

On stage, Patterson riffed about how weird it felt to stumble into this sort of success, a granted wish from a lamp he never rubbed. “I know how huge it is, but understand something: I’m 26, and I’m black,” he told the crowd. “I’ve never seen the show. I have no idea what the fuck I signed up for.”

Now in his second season of SNL, he has a better idea, a better handle on the rhythms of the schedule, a grip on the pace, a sense of which writers to work closely with. “They kind of throw you into the fire, but I like that,” he says on a September afternoon at a rooftop restaurant in midtown Manhattan. He’s eating pretzel bites instead of the watermelon-and-feta dish we wanted but decided against because of the optics. He’s wearing an Aime Leon Dore T-shirt, Ksubi jeans, and a chunky silver chain, a gift from UFC fighter Suga Sean O'Malley after Patterson kept him from losing an even more expensive piece of jewelry at a party. (O'Malley dropped his $20,000 watch and didn’t notice; Patterson heroically pointed it out.) “When I start doing anything in my life, I’d rather you throw me into the deep end,” Patterson says, “and I can try to figure out how to swim.”
Jacket and pants PUBLIC SCHOOL, top NOAH

Feeling more settled comes in part from — in his act — highlighting how absurd it is that he’s here in the first place, a 27-year-old only six years into his standup career, a fish not just out of water but swimming around in champagne. (More from “Kill Tony”: “I was on national television doing this,” he said, throwing his limbs around, grinning. “I’ve shot at somebody before. Can you understand how crazy that change is?”) It’s not just that Patterson is black or young, but it’s where he’s from. Stand-up comics, like their rapper cousins, are products of their environment, influenced by and inflected with the stuff they breathed or saw or heard when they were young. Patterson is straight Orlando, a country cousin with beach access. He’s a man from Florida, not a Florida Man, and he’s proud of it. He grew up in Ocoee, just west of the city. “Orlando got a lot of dope things coming out,” he says. “We had a decent music scene until people started going to jail,” he adds, explaining that a RICO order on the city just “took everybody.”

Both Orlando and Austin informed Patterson’s raunchy comedic style. (Austin is not only a new comedy frontier but, to some, a nasty one; critics say the city’s style tends to be crass and offensive and conservative.) “I’m very different from the usual,” he says. “I’m a rough-around-the-edges type person. I say all the words.” He brings a welcome energy to Studio 8H. “Kam is a happy and grateful young man, and that’s something that adds a lot to the environment of the show,” says his castmate Marcello Hernández.
Top CALVIN KLEIN, sweater NANAMICA
Jacket and pants PUBLIC SCHOOL, top NOAH, shoes UGG

Patterson’s comedy builds on his contrasts: off-color commentary in sweet, cuddly packaging, like a Sour Patch Kid or Seth MacFarlane’s Ted. “They was calling me all type of conservative online, and I say, ‘I vote what my mama vote for, and my mama is a strong black lady.’ I tell people, ‘Don’t take everything I say when it comes to comedy at face value, just for the simple fact that I didn’t know that a pickle was a cucumber until like a year ago.’”

Up close, Patterson is all energy but total focus. He starts six new sentences a minute but never forgets my name. He was diagnosed with ADHD as a kid. To describe his own brain, he references the episode of SpongeBob SquarePants wherein the title character is unable to recall his own name, and the little office workers running around inside his skull panic and catch on fire.
Jacket and pants STOFFA, shoes UGG

Patterson watched a lot of cartoons growing up — Danny Phantom, The Fairly OddParents — and realized he could make people laugh at a young and malleable age. And it wasn’t just people — Patterson would make up long, crazy stories about his little league football seasons, and his cool older cousins would die laughing. One night, one cousin handed him a piece of paper intended to be a ticket to Patterson’s show. “That was super cool to me,” he says, of gaining their respect. In elementary school, his teacher let him stand in front of the class and tell jokes if he completed his schoolwork.

Patterson started stand-up in earnest when he was 22 and quickly made a name for himself in the Florida scene. This satisfied him, but then one day he met Uncle Lazer, an Austin-based comic. (“He is the definition of a nigga from Texas,” Patterson says, then hears himself. “He white, but somebody from Texas.”) Lazer saw Patterson’s set and encouraged him to move to a city with a bigger scene lest he be pigeonholed as “the Florida guy.” Patterson saved up a month’s worth of paychecks and set out for the Lone Star State. It was his first time there, and he spent it knocking on the doors of comedy clubs, trying to find someone who would give him a few minutes. Once he did, he killed.
Top, sweater, and pants BOTTEGA VENETA, shoes UGG

After moving to Austin, he worked odd jobs and did open mics, regularly putting his name in the hat for “Kill Tony.” When he was eventually selected, it felt like a miracle. He’d been trying for months. He told a joke about growing up in a roach-infested home, inviting a date over and having to surreptitiously kill the bugs before she saw them. She eventually did, but she waved it away, saying that she had roaches, too. “And I’m like, ‘Ew, that’s disgusting,’” Patterson says.

He got into the rotation, then was asked to be a regular, which meant he had one minute to tell one new joke every week. He did this for two years, a veritable comedy degree. But that doesn’t mean he’s lazy. He cites the LeBron James quote about how winning is a curse: “It doesn’t matter how much you’ve won before. You’re not a winner until you win again and again and again.”
Jacket, top, and pants LOUIS VUITTON

Before getting hired on SNL, he was cast in 72 Hours, a Kevin Hart bro-comedy, alongside future coworkers Hernandez and Ben Marshall. It was a career high for Patterson, who loves Hart so much that he read Hart’s memoir, twice. (Sometimes, Hart would give Patterson a piece of advice, and he’d gleefully recall it from Hart’s book.) “The main reason I do stand-up is because, in middle school, a girl was like, ‘Nigga, you think you Kevin Hart or something?’” he says. “And I’m like,” — he affects bashfulness, batting his eyes like Bambi — “‘Maybe I do.’”

Historically, SNL’s improv-trained cast members have an easier time getting cast in writers’ sketches, and the stand-up comics are more likely to create a sketch around their own joke or formulate a “Weekend Update” monologue. Patterson’s strength is in the latter zone. A recent episode featured him pretending to be a major fan of Ryan Murphy’s Glee (“I’m a Gluniac! I’ve been Glooning all day!”). Michael Che sees through the charade and encourages him to be himself, to talk about what he actually wants to talk about. Patterson is game. “Can I talk about the time I got robbed during a threesome?” Nope. “OK, what about how I’ve never voted in my life?” No. “I got a fun story about me going to a strip club? Let me set the scene. I was 14 years old…” Che waves him off.

Patterson describes himself as an avid student of his craft; an ideal night involves performing for five minutes at six different comedy clubs. But his funny is innate, so natural it’s almost an affliction. He talks, and you laugh. It helps that he is an accomplished cusser, in the game since he was eight, when his dad gave him permission. “My dad was like, ‘Well, you small and you can’t fight, but you can do two things: You can cuss real good to get them scared of you, and you can bite them if they put their hands on you.”
Top CALVIN KLEIN, shirt and pants MFPEN, jacket DIOR, shoes UGG

But what’s cool about SNL is that it’s a group sport, after years of performing solo. Among Patterson’s favorite writing partners are “the Harvard boys,” Tucker Flodman and Maxwell Gay. “I went to the office the first day and I was just like” — he deepens his voice into a growl and slams his hands on the table— “y’all writing for me now.” “I don’t write," he says. "I kind of spew things out, and they take my shit in my mind and put it into a format that’s suitable for the show. That’s what I really enjoy about SNL: the teamwork.”

The day before our interview, Patterson bought his first journal. “People always say either do that or go to therapy, and I don’t want to talk to nobody, so I started writing,” he says. “My dreams are so vast and insane in my mind. I don’t feel like I’m there yet. It’s nice, where I am, it’s a blessing to be here. But I don’t feel like I’m chasing some crazy shit.”
Top CALVIN KLEIN, shirt MFPEN
Top, sweater, and pants BOTTEGA VENETA, shoes UGG

One of his dreams is to buy a town, “some Walt Disney-type shit, like Celebration, Florida.” It’s a plan inspired by Dave Chappelle who, in an effort toward economic revitalization, has purchased a significant number of businesses and land in his hometown in Ohio. Only recently did Patterson learn about the 1920 Ocoee Election Day Massacre, when the Ku Klux Klan murdered 50 black residents for attempting to vote, and he thinks it’d be nice to give back to the community and invest in local economies. But then, he has taller mountains to climb. “I can’t wait to say ‘nigga’ on TV,” he says, a wicked smile in his eyes. “One day, they gonna let me.”
Movement Director: Ash Rucker
Photographed by: Luisa Opalesky
PA: Kenny La Rosa, Matthew Sheehan, Ben Jones
Styling Assistant: Ola Olajide

items.title: Is the Luxury Fleece Era Over?
items.description: As the inimitable A$AP “Lord Pretty Flacko Jodye” Rocky once rapped in “Fashion Killa,” his 2013 magnum opus: “She got a lot of Prada. That Dolce & Gabbana. I can't forget Escada. And that Balenciaga.” He’d also name-check Alexander Wang, Helmut Lang, Cartier,
items.author: Chris Erik Thomas
paragraphs: As the inimitable A$AP “Lord Pretty Flacko Jodye” Rocky once rapped in “Fashion Killa,” his 2013 magnum opus: “She got a lot of Prada. That Dolce & Gabbana. I can't forget Escada. And that Balenciaga.” He’d also name-check Alexander Wang, Helmut Lang, Cartier, and even Donna Karan.

Were he to write “Fashion Killa” today, another far more random brand would likely show up: Alo. Yes, that Alo. The LA athleisure brand beloved for its leggings and made famous by Kendall Jenner, Hailey Bieber, and Bella Hadid (and occasionally an NFLer like Joe Burrow).

A Rocky co-sign is unexpected if you’re not paying attention to the moves Mr. Rihanna is making, but the man is loving the brand. He wore a white Alo Accolade quarter-zip in an Instagram post this week (announcing he’s guest-judging the social network’s Bode-approved awards) and wore the same pullover in navy post-Met Gala in May, styled with Prada sneakers and a Chanel backpack.

Seeing someone of Rocky’s stature wear an Alo fleece, when he’s so often seen in major labels, is as much a sign as it is a reason to do a postmortem on the cultural dominance of something like that viral $910 fleece. (Which, hey, at least that one’s 100% wool.) Compare Alo’s $148 cotton-polyester sweater to a stylistically comparable Miu-Miu half-zip, which is $2,450 and made entirely of polyester.

Houston, we have a problem. The bottom of the cozy-luxe fleece market has fallen out. Even the proudly expensive fleece is on deep discount. Seasonal sales happen all the time, of course, but it hits different when they include products whose price was meant to signal exclusivity. Meanwhile, more affordable brands like Alo — and Zara, and COS — are hiring superstar photographers like Steven Meisel for their campaigns and staging full-on runway shows.
Luxury isn’t going anywhere (and I’m sure Rocky still adores his Dior), but he’s also helping dispel the idea that a fleece needs to cost close to a grand to be worth buying.

items.title: В Краснодарском аэропорту нашли пропавшего более месяца назад кота
items.description: В аэропорту Краснодара обнаружили сбежавшего перед рейсом кота
items.author: Александра Копылова
paragraphs: В аэропорту Краснодара обнаружили сбежавшего перед рейсом кота
В Краснодарском аэропорту нашли кота Василия, который пропал перед рейсом в Грузию в сентябре. Об этом сообщили в телеграм-канале аэровокзала.

Кота искали больше месяца. Вечером 23 сентября он выбрался из переноски во время подготовки к рейсу в Батуми. В Red Wings тогда заявили, что готовы бесплатно доставить Василия его хозяйке, когда его найдут.

Весь месяц работники аэропорта искали питомца. 27 октября сотрудница службы наземного обслуживания услышала мяуканье, благодаря чему кота удалось найти. Хозяйка животного находится в Батуми. С ней связались, она подтвердила, что это Василий.
В аэропорту отметили, что с котом всё хорошо. Представители Red Wings помогут организовать Василия отправку в Батуми, а до этого он побудет у сестры владелицы.
Ранее во Франции нашли кота, который сбежал из дома 12 лет назад ещё котёнком. Его заметили среди бродячих котов в 60 км от дома. Найти владельцев удалось по микрочипу.

items.title: Apple бесплатно заменит iPhone Duo с трещинами на экране
items.description: Apple бесплатно заменит iPhone Duo с трещинами на экране
items.author: Иван Адоньев
paragraphs: Apple бесплатно заменит iPhone Duo с трещинами на экране
Apple бесплатно заменит смартфоны iPhone Duo, у которых появились трещины на внутреннем дисплее. Компания признала проблему, затронувшую небольшое количество устройств, передаёт Reuters.

Покупатели начали сообщать о неисправностях вскоре после выхода смартфона. Некоторые пользователи слышали хруст при раскрытии устройства, после чего вдоль центрального сгиба экрана появлялась крупная трещина.

Apple заявила, что в затронутых устройствах дефект проявляется быстро. Владельцам таких смартфонов рекомендовали обратиться в AppleCare для замены. Возможную причину неисправности компания не назвала.

iFixit создала трёхмерную модель шарнирного механизма iPhone Duo и сопоставила её с местами появления повреждений. По версии компании, проблема может быть связана с центральной опорной планкой рядом со шлейфом дисплея.
Специалисты предположили, что при складывании планка может смещаться неправильно и создавать повышенное напряжение в области шлейфа. Apple выводы iFixit не комментировала.
При этом в iFixit назвали iPhone Duo самым ремонтопригодным складным смартфоном из протестированных компанией.
iPhone Duo поступил в продажу 23 октября и стал первым складным смартфоном Apple.

items.title: Елена Мясникова: Мы возвращаем природу человеку
items.description: Представьте проходную, корпуса и график смен. Красота здесь не предусмотрена даже техзаданием. И вдруг среди бетона появляется сквер со скамьями-качелями на цепях, водоёмом и светом, под который предлагают медитировать. Автор, куратор «Архстояния» в Никола-Лен
items.author: Елена Мясникова
paragraphs: Представьте проходную, корпуса и график смен. Красота здесь не предусмотрена даже техзаданием. И вдруг среди бетона появляется сквер со скамьями-качелями на цепях, водоёмом и светом, под который предлагают медитировать. Автор, куратор «Архстояния» в Никола-Ленивце, называет сквер «мягкой лакуной» в угловатом теле технополиса. Я ждала лавочку и урну с претензией на концепцию, а получила микрофлору, альфа-ритмы и швейцарского архитектора, который охлаждает парки. Спрашиваю, зачем всё это людям, окружённым станками и серверами.
Почему именно здесь нужны отдых, игра и даже медитация?

Территории технополисов по инициативе мэрии превращаются в среду не только для работы, но и для отдыха, причём для горожан тоже. Человеку нужно переключаться после умственной, а порой и нервной нагрузки. Главное, чтобы он чувствовал себя в безопасности — и этически, и эстетически.

Промышленная среда думает о процессе, а не о человеке. Но человек не робот: паузы нужны мозгу, и это подтвердит любой физиолог. Унылая среда влияет на настроение и поведение, в ней не хочется работать. А высококвалифицированные кадры выбирают место не только по зарплате. Где ещё неформально поговорить с коллегой или прийти в себя после переговоров? В мире в технологических компаниях строят инфраструктуру, из которой не хочется уходить. Антон вспоминает китайский Beijing Xingfa и ереванский офис JetBrains с садом для медитации.
Сквер построен как чашка Петри. Значит, вы выращиваете человеку микрофлору?
Сравнение подходящее. Это чашка Петри, увеличенная в десятки раз. Очагами микрофлоры служат клумбы, водоём, игровые зоны и качели, а бортом чаши стало мультимедийное кольцо.
Как не превратить всё это в набор развлечений?

Элементы связаны, как сообщество организмов. А для посетителя прописан сценарий, от активного к созерцательному. Сначала пинг-понг и балансир, потом медленные качели, затем медитация в световом кольце и наблюдение за деревьями.

Сначала хотелось организовать границу покоя, ведь сквер должен быть точкой покоя. Границей стал тонкий кольцевой элемент на частых колоннах. Потом к работе над светом и экранами был приглашен мультимедиа-художник Алексея Новикова и студия Savin Lab.
Вы запрограммировали его на тета-, альфа- и бета-ритмы. Должен ли архитектор знать нейрофизиологию?
Не настаиваю, это мой выбор, когда работаю с концепцией покоя. Пришлось залезть в нейробиологию. Для другой концепции залезу в другую науку и что-нибудь интересное оттуда достану.
Где кончается архитектура и начинается терапия?

Я не хочу проводить эту границу. Плавные линии рельефа напоминают поля и леса, которые с первобытных времён успокаивают. Вода снимает судорожность мысли. А скамьи-качели — это же укачивание ребёнка, чем не терапия?
Нужно ли уметь медитировать, чтобы воспользоваться кольцом?
Навыки не нужны. Нужно создать намерение хотя бы одиннадцать минут не отвлекаться и не беспокоиться.

Одиннадцать минут без беспокойства. Для московского офисного человека это, пожалуй, самое амбициозное требование во всём проекте, куда сложнее любых альфа-ритмов. Впрочем, выйти из-под воздействия кольца проще простого: достаточно перестать на него смотреть. Это не кинотеатр, а полметровая полоса экранов. Режимов несколько. В базовом свет мерцает как огонь в камине, чего нам так не хватает российскими зимами. А летом лёгкий пар увлажняет воздух.
Вы работаете со всеми органами чувств?

Это давнее стремление и обязательное условие качественной работы. Двадцать один год в Никола-Ленивце я в этом убеждаюсь. Мой любимый зарубежный архитектор Филипп Рамм вообще строит на не визуальном. В тайваньском парке он охладил одну зону, а в другой сделал так, чтобы не летели комары.
Архитектор, который отменил комаров, достоин памятника. Мечтаю, чтобы эту технологию внедрили на даче, а почему терравей, а не обычный гравий?

Тактильность — неотъемлемое качество архитектуры. Гравийный отсев хорош, но плохо себя ведёт у воды и при сложной геометрии. Терравей — тот же отсев, только склеенный и утрамбованный, поэтому удобнее для ходьбы.
Сосны, ели, рябины, клёны, сирень. Это среднерусский пейзаж?
Мы взяли дары нашей полосы, но важно было соблюсти разнообразие пород, как в природе. Контраст со стальной и бетонной архитектурой есть, а конфликта нет. Мы возвращаем природу человеку.
А пинг-понг? Вы сомневались, что взрослые занятые люди станут играть?

Да, когда аналитики по опросам предложили полуспортивное оборудование, у меня были сомнения. Но к концу стройки резиденты сами спрашивали, когда можно будет играть. Нельзя постоянно работать головой и не встряхивать тело.
Чем этот проект отличается от Никола-Ленивца?

Там люди едут за опытом специально, а здесь выходят на перерыв. Но принцип тот же: вовлечь человека в природную естественность через геометрию, зелень, покрытия и свет. Общественное пространство сегодня нужно не только для отдыха, но и для психологической помощи.

Вы назвали этот проект прецедентом для Москвы: точка релаксации среди промышленных корпусов. Почему именно сегодня человеку, который работает в технологической среде, особенно необходимо такое пространство?

Промышленная среда это место, где в первую очередь рассматривается процесс производства — потребностям человека в общественном пространстве здесь не место. Эстетические потребности вообще не рассматриваются.
Но человек это не робот и не машина. Между работой нужно делать паузы — так лучше работает мозг и тело остается в тонусе. Вам об этом скажет любой физиолог.
Есть и эстетические потребности — степень унылости среды влияет на настроение и даже поведение и отношение пользователя: в унылой среде — нет желания находиться и работать.

Критерий качественного общественного пространства усугубляется еще и тем, что в технополисе сосредотачивается выскотехнологичное производство, где как в наукограде происходят не только конвеерные, но и сложные, нелинейные процессы, требующие от работников разного интеллектуального опыта, что требует высококвалифицированных кадров, то есть людей востребованных, которые при выборе места работы смотрят не только на зарплаты, но и на другие возможности. Окружающая среда среди этих возможностей занимает не последнее место: где еще можно пообщаться с коллегой неформально, где переключиться после напряжения или переговоров?

Мировой опыт благоустройства технологических компаний и наукоградов давно уже шагнул к созданию полноценной инфраструктуры, главной задачей которой состоит в том чтобы работнику в ней было хорошо, чтобы не хотелось из нее выходить. Возьмем в пример китайский BEIJING XINGFA или хотя бы Ереванский офис Jetbrains, где создано все для полноценного существования внутри комплекса, вплоть до сада для медитации.

Вот так, по инициативе правительства Москвы Территория технополисов преобразовывается в среду не только для работы, но и для отдыха и работы, причем не только для работников, но и для горожан. На мой взгляд, полноценная среда, где работник может переключиться с умственной иногда нервной загрузки, может являться местом игры, отдыха, общения и медитации. Главное, чтобы посетитель ощущал безопасность, как этическую, так и эстетическую внутри этого пространства.

items.title: В Москве выберут десять лучших ресторанов столицы по версии WHERETOEAT
items.description: В Москве пройдёт церемония ресторанной премии WHERETOEAT Москва 2026
items.author: Виолетта Ефимова
paragraphs: В Москве пройдёт церемония ресторанной премии WHERETOEAT Москва 2026

6 ноября в московском Lotte Hotel Moscow пройдёт XI церемония вручения ресторанной премии WHERETOEAT Москва 2026. На мероприятии объявят десять лучших ресторанов столицы и победителей специальных номинаций.

В лонг-лист этого года вошли более 100 заведений, представляющих разные направления московской гастрономии. Среди них — авторские рестораны, проекты современной русской кухни, итальянские траттории, азиатские концепции, а также рестораны, специализирующиеся на мясе и морепродуктах.

Помимо основного рейтинга, организаторы вручат награды в восьми специальных номинациях. Среди них — «Шеф-повар года», «Женщина шеф-повар года», «Шеф-кондитер года», «Сомелье года», «Бар года» и «Выбор СМИ». Также отметят ресторан с лучшей пивной картой по версии бренда «Балтика» и победителя номинации «We Fry с огнём внутри».

Рейтинг составляют по итогам тайного голосования коллегии из 100 экспертов. В неё входят представители ресторанного и гостиничного бизнеса, винной индустрии и профильных медиа. Имена победителей станут известны во время церемонии.
В 2025 году первое место занял ресторан Olluco, второе — «За крышей», третье — Sage.

Московская церемония продолжит осенний сезон WHERETOEAT в России. В этом году награждения проходят в семи гастрономических регионах страны. Завершится сезон 12 ноября церемонией WHERETOEAT Северо-Запад в Санкт-Петербурге.

С 2026 года премия получила международный статус, в ней участвуют семь стран — Россия, Беларусь, Казахстан, Азербайджан, Армения, Грузия и Узбекистан. По итогам национальных голосований сформируют единый евро-азиатский рейтинг WHERETOEAT INTERNATIONAL 2027. Его церемония запланирована на апрель.
