items.title: Iowa’s GOP Candidate for Governor Might Not Live in Iowa
items.description: The term carpetbagger was originally applied to Northerners who moved South after the Civil War to launch political careers under the protection of military Reconstruction; it referred to the hastily procured bags manufactured from carpet scraps the transplant
items.author: Ed Kilgore
paragraphs: The term carpetbagger was originally applied to Northerners who moved South after the Civil War to launch political careers under the protection of military Reconstruction; it referred to the hastily procured bags manufactured from carpet scraps the transplants allegedly used. More recently, the term has been applied to politicians who conveniently relocate themselves into the vicinity of political opportunities. New York has often been a magnet for alleged carpetbaggers. In the 1960s alone, two former U.S. attorneys general, Robert F. Kennedy and Ramsey Clark, moved to the Empire State and ran for the Senate (the former successfully, the latter not so much), and a generation later, so did former Arkansas First Lady Hillary Clinton (like RFK, she won).

So in itself, the decision by conservative ex-lobbyist and businessman Zach Lahn to move from Kansas to Iowa in 2024 and then run for governor — winning the 2026 GOP primary in a big upset — isn’t so remarkable. Indeed, Lahn was born and grew up in Iowa, where his family had lived for generations, and owned property there.

What has made his case interesting — and for supporters of his Democratic opponent, Rob Sand, hilarious — is his difficulty making a clean break with it. He seems very involved in Kansas matters. He remains president of the board of an unaccredited Wichita private school he co-founded with his wife, albeit when they were both married to other people (in her case to a scion of the Kansas Koch family empire, with whom she financed the Wonder School, as they called it). And the children from the blended families he and his wife left in Kansas have given Lahn a reason to fly his private plane back to Wichita a lot — at least 37 times since he began running for governor, according to the Des Moines Register. But that isn’t the only evidence that Lahn has Kansas on his mind. Last month, the Daily Beast reported that a Strava fitness-app user with the name “Zach Lahn” recorded four long bike rides starting at Lahn’s Wichita estate over three months in early 2025, long after his supposed relocation to Iowa.

Perhaps more eyebrow-raising have been his public musings over the amount of time he’ll need to spend away from Iowa’s capital if he does become the governor of the Hawkeye State. “We’ve already had discussions about this and how that would work,” he told the Register in May. “But if I’m elected governor, it would be a different arrangement, and we’d work it out. Because, you know, we’d be in Iowa as much as humanly possible.”

That has to be comforting, but it certainly hasn’t quelled questions about Lahn’s state loyalties, considering his campaign’s Trump-modeled message is “Iowa First.” Or at least since October 17, 2024, which was when he transferred his voter registration to the state. You’re required to have Iowa residency for at least two years to run for governor there, so he got in just under the wire.
Unsurprisingly, Lahn’s shaky status as an Iowan has been bread and meat for Sand’s campaign, which has offered him Iowa travel tips:
And even more cleverly, Sand’s backers got Kansas’s Democratic governor Laura Kelly in on the action:

When Lahn first decided to run, his “outsider” status might have seemed like a positive credential. The current two-term Republican governor of Iowa, Kim Reynolds, is deeply unpopular (for many months, she’s reigned as “America’s most unpopular governor” according to polling from Morning Consult). So while he was campaigning in the primary against Iowa GOP Establishment candidate Randy Feenstra, Lahn made a logical choice by separating himself from the usual suspects in Des Moines and Washington. But Wichita is a little too “outside” Iowa for comfort. And in explaining the details of his family situation, Lahn has also drawn attention to his not entirely orthodox relationship with the insanely rich and controversial Koch family (for whom he worked as an Americans for Prosperity operative before marrying Chase Koch’s ex-wife). He’s not just any old dad with custody issues.

Other than the poor management of his residential status, Lahn was unlucky to have made his move back to Iowa for what is turning out to be a strong Democratic year in a state that turned deep red in 2014 and has remained so ever since. Democrats have even odds of winning the Senate seat being vacated by Joni Ernst and could flip three of Iowa’s four U.S. House seats as well. In Sand, the sole member of his party in statewide office, Democrats have a solidly established centrist candidate who is difficult for the GOP to label as a “radical” or “socialist” (though it has tried). Lahn has sought to adopt a populist stance by criticizing both major party establishments and has a MAHA strain in his ideology that has enabled him to attack polluters with whom Republicans often snuggle. The two candidates are more or less evenly matched financially.

In part because of a vast advantage in name ID, Sand has led Lahn in public polling from the get-go. In the Silver Bulletin polling averages, Sand leads by a robust 7.3 percent, though the most recent polls show the race tightening a bit. As in other midwestern states, Democrats are nervous about possible polling errors (Iowa is, after all, where the legendary pollster Ann Selzer infamously showed Kamala Harris leading Trump in 2024). The Trump administration, meanwhile, is working overtime to deliver tasty treats (e.g., fuel assistance to hard-pressed farmers and a new federally assisted steel mill) to Iowa voters.

If Sand nonetheless prevails, Republicans will naturally wonder if a more Iowa-centric candidate like Feenstra might have won. And Lahn may wonder whether he picked the wrong “home state” for his gubernatorial dreams.

items.title: Jay-Z to Perform at Apple Music 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show
items.description: Jay-Z is slated to perform at the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show, taking place on Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.
items.author: Steven J Horowitz
paragraphs: Jay-Z is slated to perform at the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show, taking place on Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” said Jay-Z in a statement. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

The announcement comes on the heels of an anniversary victory lap this year under the banner “Jay-Z 30.” He kicked off the celebrations as a headliner at the Roots Picnic in late May, followed by three sold-out shows at Yankee Stadium in July to honor the 25th and 30th anniversaries of his albums “The Blueprint” and “Reasonable Doubt,” respectively. In addition to international shows in Paris and London, Jay sat down with Rick Rubin for the eight-part docuseries “Jay-Z in 8” where he broke down hits and deep cuts across his catalog. This past weekend, he brought his global string of tour dates to a close at SoFi Stadium with two nights featuring guest appearances from Scarface, DJ Khaled, John Legend, Blue Ivy Carter, Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too Short.

“For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” said NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell in a statement. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”

“Jay-Z’s impact on global music culture is as profound as it is undeniable,” added Oliver Schusser, Apple’s Vice President of Music and International Content. “We’ve had the privilege of working closely with him these last few years to bring some of the world’s most exciting and prolific artists to the Super Bowl Halftime Show stage and we are so thrilled that he will be taking that stage himself this year. We know it’s going to be an incredible show.”

The Super Bowl Halftime Show will air on ESPN, ABC and Disney+, and on mobile devices with NFL+. ESPN’s Spanish-language telecast will also be available on ESPN Deportes and Disney+, with a separate Spanish-language presentation on Univision. Roc Nation will executive produce the show, while Hamish Hamilton will serve as director.

Earlier this year, Bad Bunny held court as the Super Bowl Halftime Show performer, celebrating his Puerto Rican heritage in the tradition of Latin America. The elaborate set included a mock sugar-cane field and a Puerto Rican vecindad with a barber shop, liquor store and a casita where Bad Bunny welcomed celebrity guests including Jessica Alba, Karol G, Cardi B, Young Miko and Pedro Pascal, among others. Bad Bunny also brought out surprise artists Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin for a salsa-inflected version of “Die With a Smile” and “lo que le pasó a Hawái,” respectively.

The Benito Bowl, as it was affectionately dubbed by his fans, reached an average of 128.2 million viewers, above the 124.9 million average viewers achieved by the Super Bowl overall but down from the 133.5 million viewers reached by Kendrick Lamar in 2025. Before Lamar, Usher held the record for most viewers with his 2024 performance.

Last month, Bad Bunny won his first Emmy for his Super Bowl Halftime Show performance in the outstanding special (live) category. The spectacle took home a total of seven wins, including musical direction, choreography, sound mixing, lighting design, technical direction/camerawork and directing.

Speaking about the performance, creative director Harriet Cuddeford previously told Variety, “The performance is celebrating normal people, and what it is to be human and love and have joy, and really appreciate one another. This was to show how much he values his community, to celebrate normal people on the world’s biggest stage, especially people who are of importance in Latino culture. He’s a very authentic person, Benito, and it’s about just being authentic and very real and very human.”

In addition to the aforementioned artists, recent performers at the Super Bowl Halftime Show have included Rihanna, the Weeknd and a collective performance from Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, Lamar, 50 Cent and Anderson .Paak.

items.title: How ‘You Can See Everything’ Became a Surprise Box Office Hit (and Likely One of the Biggest Docs of All Time)
items.description: “You Can See Everything” has remained a must-see at the box office, collecting a remarkable $19.5 million from 2,655 theaters in its second weekend — a notable increase in ticket sales from its sizable opening.
items.author: Rebecca Rubin
paragraphs: “You Can See Everything” has remained a must-see at the box office, collecting a remarkable $19.5 million from 2,655 theaters in its second weekend — a notable increase in ticket sales from its sizable opening.

A24‘s buzzy documentary about Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes has grossed $45.1 million domestically to date and will be very profitable for the studio against a lean $7 million budget. With electric word-of-mouth, awards chatter and repeat viewings from audiences who are trying to make sense of what they saw on screen, the movie should remain a big-screen draw through the fall. It’s primed to leave theaters as one of the biggest non-musical documentaries of all time, a true feat for a nearly three-hour film that wasn’t publicized until a month before debuting in cinemas. Right now, “Michael Jackson’s This Is It” is the highest-grossing documentary ever with $267 million in 2009, not adjusted for inflation. Meanwhile Michael Moore’s “Fahrenheit 9/11” is the biggest non-music doc with $222 million in 2004, followed by two nature films, “March of the Penguins” with $127 million in 2005 and “Earth” with $107 million in 2007. “You Can See Everything” needs to become a hit overseas to crack the top five.
After a strong second weekend in North America, here are four takeaways from the surprise success of “You Can See Everything.”
Restraint bolstered demand

A24 began rolling out “You Can See Everything” in 855 theaters, a huge footprint for a documentary. (By comparison, Bleecker Street launched “Musk,” a four-hour look at the world’s richest man, in four locations.) The film opened to $15.6 million — thanks to the more than 2,000 sold-out showings — as cinephiles rushed to theaters to avoid spoilers; the stranger-than-fiction story follows Holmes right before she begins her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. The decision to launch the movie in moderate release — rather than limited in just a handful of venues or nationwide on more than 2,000 screens — proved wise because the studio was able to bolster awareness while cultivating a sense of scarcity. (In New York City and Los Angeles, good luck catching the film during its first weekend in theaters if you didn’t buy a seat way in advance.) Then ticket sales climbed by 28% as “You Can See Everything” expanded to 2,666 theaters in its second weekend, underscoring the film’s genuine commercial viability beyond the coasts.

“Opening ‘You Can See Everything’ in 855 theaters was a really smart move, allowing the film to establish itself and build momentum before going much wider,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian. “The fact that we’re seeing a documentary deliver such a significant second-weekend increase is remarkable.”
Secrecy around the project dialed up the anticipation

Nobody knew about the existence of “You Can See Everything” until its surprise world premiere at the Telluride Film Festival in early September. (That’s nothing short of a miracle in Hollywood, where even your waiter knows your P&A spend.) In the scenic Colorado mountain town, the movie became a word-of-mouth sensation after garnering near-euphoric reviews. Shrouding the film in secrecy became an effective marketing tactic. After all, there’s no shortage of movies and television shows about Holmes. Her rise and spectacular fall from grace has been depicted in the Hulu series “The Dropout,” starring Amanda Seyfried, as well as Gibney’s “The Inventor: Out for Blood in Silicon Valley.” But the immediate sense around “You Can See Everything” was that co-directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim had captured something very, very different. (And many felt that Holmes had met her match in Fielder, a cringe comedy master best known for HBO’s “The Rehearsal.”)

“Bear in mind, the project started with no blueprint or screenplay for how to tell this story,” says analyst David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “A24 invested in an interesting but complicated idea without a beginning, middle or end. That’s turned into a zeitgeist film about money, dreams, truth and reality.”
Word-of-mouth elevated ticket sales in the movie’s second weekend

“You Can See Everything” surged in its second weekend because there was quality to match the hype. Some 90% of initial ticket buyers say they would “definitely recommend” the film and 80% said the movie was “even better than expected,” according to exit polls. On social media, people who saw the movie were encouraging others to seek out packed theaters so they could share in the wild reactions and insane twists and turns of the story with others. From “Michael” to “Obsession” to “The Odyssey,” there’s been at least one commonality between many of this year’s box office hits: They’re fun to watch with crowds.
Younger audiences are all in on A24

Roughly 70% of opening weekend ticket buyers were under 35, an unexpectedly youthful turnout for a non-fiction film. However, it’s not surprising for A24, which has cultivated a loyal, young demographic over the years through edgy, aesthetic arthouse favorites like “Marty Supreme” and “Everything Everywhere All at Once.” This year’s lineup of “The Drama,” “Backrooms” and “Primetime” also scored for the indie studio after reaching event-status for Gen Zers. That’s not to say they’ll show up for anything from A24. Chris Rock’s Hollywood-set dramedy “Misty Green” and Hugh Jackman’s revisionist adventure “The Death of Robin Hood” were two recent releases from A24 that misfired in theaters.

items.title: Jay-Z to Headline 2027 Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show
items.description: Jay-Z has been tapped to headline the 2027 Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show.
items.author: Carly Thomas; Abid Rahman
paragraphs: Jay-Z has been tapped to headline the 2027 Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show.
He follows in the footsteps of Grammy-winning artist Bad Bunny, who made his mark during Super Bowl LX earlier this year with his Emmy-winning performance.

The news was announced during halftime of the Cowboys vs. Eagles Monday Night Football game. “It will be Jay-Z in SoFi on [Valentine’s Day],” ABC commentator Scott Van Pelt said. “We’ll all be looking forward to seeing that.”
“He is the GOAT,” analyst Jason Kelce added. “He’s got more stadium-ready hits than most artists have songs, period. Should be a great show.”

“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” Jay-Z said in a statement. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

“For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” added NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”

“Jay-Z’s impact on global music culture is as profound as it is undeniable,” said Oliver Schusser, Apple’s vp of music and international content, in a statement. “We’ve had the privilege of working closely with him these last few years to bring some of the world’s most exciting and prolific artists to the Super Bowl Halftime Show stage and we are so thrilled that he will be taking that stage himself this year. We know it’s going to be an incredible show.”

Jimmy Pitaro, ESPN Chairman, added: “Jay-Z has been setting a standard of excellence for decades, as an artist, a cultural force and a winner of 25 Grammy Awards. The Super Bowl is already a defining moment in music, and his performance will be the latest milestone in a career synonymous with success. We look forward to showcasing the highly anticipated halftime set in the U.S. and around the world across our platforms, including on ESPN, ABC and Disney+.”

Jay-Z joins a coveted list of artists who have earned the opportunity to headline the NFL’s biggest night, including his wife Beyoncé, Bad Bunny, Kendrick Lamar, Michael Jackson, Rihanna, Madonna, Lady Gaga, Bruce Springsteen, Diana Ross, Katy Perry, The Weeknd, Usher, The Rolling Stones and Bruno Mars, among many others.

The billionaire rap icon already curates the Halftime Show through his company Roc Nation in a deal with the NFL that began in 2019 and was renewed in 2024. Given his close connections with NFL powerbrokers, it was inevitable that Jay-Z would pick himself at some point to headline the marquee event.
Super Bowl LXI will air on ABC and ESPN. The game will take place Sunday, Feb. 14, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, home of the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers.

Back in February, Bad Bunny brought his Latin love to the Super Bowl stage, turning Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California, into a big dance party. During his 13-minute set, he performed a wide range of his biggest hits, including “Tití Me Preguntó,” “Eoo,” “BAILE INoLVIDABLE,” “El Apagón,” “CAFé CON RON,” “MONACO,” NUEVAYoL” and “DtMF,” among others.

The Puerto Rican rapper and singer also told a love story throughout the performance, which included several celebrity cameos, and ended with a message of unity and love displayed on the screens inside the stadium, which read, “The only thing more powerful than hate is love.”

Jay-Z and the NFL first linked up in 2019, in a deal that saw the league and Roc Nation work together on events and social activism. The NFL would consult Roc Nation on its entertainment offerings, including the Super Bowl Halftime Show, and also work with the company “strengthen community through music and the NFL’s Inspire Change initiative.”

The league working with Jay-Z came in the wake of the NFL’s controversial treatment of former San Francisco 49ers player Colin Kaepernick, who was effectively forced out of the NFL for staging protests against police brutality and systemic racism. The legendary rapper initially publicly supported Kaepernick in his fight against the NFL.

But after Jay-Z was brought on board to essentially revitalize the league’s brand that had taken a battering over the Kaepernick affair, the two fell out. “[Jay-Z] has built the alignment with the NFL, the NFL that has blackballed me, the same NFL that, in a players-owners meeting in 2017, said we need a Black face to help us get rid of the protests,” Kaepernick told NBC News in September 2026.
Puck was first to report the news of Jay-Z being named the headliner.
Ryan Gajewski contributed to this story.

items.title: Instagram Tests 90-Minute Horizontal Videos in Major Play for Podcasters and Creators
items.description: Instagram is testing features aimed at capturing a bigger part of the entertainment landscape, including the ability to play longform videos like podcasts and more on the platform.
items.author: Caitlin Huston
paragraphs: Instagram is testing features aimed at capturing a bigger part of the entertainment landscape, including the ability to play longform videos like podcasts and more on the platform.

Starting Monday, Instagram will be launching a test of horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes with select creators in the U.S. The product, called Features, is aimed at podcasters, comedians and other longform creators, with the ability to refer viewers to the full video from the shortform reels on the platform, which are typically around three minutes or less.

“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” said Tessa Lyons, vp product at Instagram.

Instagram has already been testing the feature with creators in Brazil and has a plan to expand to tens of thousands of creators in the U.S. The videos will also be recommended to users on Instagram’s Explore page and in other areas. Early creators involved in the test include podcast host and Skims co-founder Emma Grede; beauty and fashion creator Monet McMichael; Preston Rakovsky, who interviews New Yorkers about love and relationships; and football content creator Donald De La Haye.

This comes as Netflix, Disney and more have been adding podcasts and videos from creators to their platforms, in an effort to capture more consumer viewing hours and compete with entertainment behemoth YouTube. One challenge for Instagram and others in the battle against YouTube has been competing against the platform’s lucrative revenue-sharing deals, with YouTube offering qualified creators offered 55 percent of ad revenue and helping generate brand deals.

Lyons said Instagram is currently working on “a few different deals” with the early creators for Features, but there’s currently no exclusivity around putting the videos on Instagram (unlike Netflix’s deals for podcasts). Additionally, existing ad deals will carry over into the videos, but Instagram will also work with creators without existing placements to find deals.

“For established creators who already have those relationships, they can bring that content with those placements and that branded content. And we also think that there’s a big opportunity for us to help creators who don’t yet have that infrastructure and that business behind them,” Lyons said.

Features will be available on mobile, but the goal is to carry the viewing experience over to Instagram for TV, which launched last year with Samsung, Fire TV, Google TV and is now expanding to Apple TV in the U.S. as part of Instagram’s move for more of the entertainment landscape.

“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said.

Additionally, given the rise of microdramas, as well as a desire among creators for episodic videos, Instagram has been experimenting with Series, which provides a home for episodic Reels on a creator’s profile. In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to experiment with the feature and has since been reaching out to individual creators, who have been experimenting with their own episodic content.

In the coming months, Instagram plans to begin testing the feature in more countries and bring it to the U.S. by the end of this year or early next year. The company has also begun testing how it will appear on TV.

These join other new features Instagram has been testing out, including integrating live video into the Reels tab and showing live videos to audiences who don’t follow the users. This is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with plans to expand it to the U.S. next year.

items.title: Cool, Cool, Cool, Palmer Luckey and Ben Lamm Made a Genetically Modified Military Dog Startup
items.description: A new startup launched today with the definitely not terrifying mission of creating genetically enhanced dogs for the United States military, law enforcement, and emergency first responders.
items.author: Kate Knibbs
paragraphs: A new startup launched today with the definitely not terrifying mission of creating genetically enhanced dogs for the United States military, law enforcement, and emergency first responders.

Warhound is the brainchild of Anduril’s Palmer Luckey and Colossal Biosciences cofounder Ben Lamm. The startup has raised $200 million to “rebuild America’s domestic supply of elite working dogs” and reduce dependency on European dog breeders for military canines.

Lamm tells WIRED that Warhound is in the process of gene-editing its first batch of dogs. The startup has already collected blood samples from specific "top-performing” military, police, and first responder dogs in the United States, and its goal is to clone them. Breeds will be “mostly Belgian Malinois, some labs, and some shepherds,” he says. The company anticipates the first round of puppies to be born in early 2027.

The initial rounds of gene-editing will focus on eliminating common health conditions that impact these breeds, like hip dysplasia. Further down the line, Lamm envisions expanding to “really interesting things,” such as incorporating olfactory receptor genes from wolves to “enhance” the military dogs. (Colossal Biosciences is perhaps best known for its work on gene-edited wolves for its so-called Dire Wolf De-Extinction Project.)

Warhound, based in Texas, will also equip its canines with “Anduril’s advanced cybernetic Augments, software, and battlefield situational awareness,” according to a press release. Asked if this means the dogs will be some kind of cyborgs, Lamm clarifies that the plan right now is to supply them with tools like “advanced body armor” rather than, say, embedding some sort of computer in their dog bodies.
“So no dogs with lasers?” WIRED asked Lamm.

“I can’t comment on what Anduril plans,” he says. “Dog safety and performance, and then helping continue helping to improve the human handler and dog bond, and working as a team—that is what the mission is.”

Neither Luckey nor Lamm will be involved in Warhound’s day-to-day, although Lamm is on the company’s board, he says. David Spirk, a former Department of Defense chief data officer who most recently worked at Palantir, is serving as chief executive, and investors include In-Q-Tel, Sequoia Capital, and ARK Invest. Luckey is not an owner and does not have equity in the company, nor does Anduril; Colossal Biosciences does have an ownership stake.

Luckey and Lamm have been working on the project for over a year, Lamm says, and just recently decided to take the company out of stealth. “Someone said, ‘So it's like the Captain America dog program with the Ironman tech program on top of it,’” Lamm tells WIRED.
Everyone can agree that this is normal, and good, and that when the precision-designed beasts arrive on Earth, they will recognize that we are not the enemy.
The company plans to operate under the guidance of the American Humane Society.

items.title: My Botched Plastic Surgery ‘Down There’
items.description: It was roughly a month after my first labiaplasty and an hour into a threesome when I realized something was wrong. A finger went into my hole — or rather, a hole in my labia. The stitches holding one of my shiny new lips together had apparently failed. I rema
items.author: Jasmine Glass
paragraphs: It was roughly a month after my first labiaplasty and an hour into a threesome when I realized something was wrong. A finger went into my hole — or rather, a hole in my labia. The stitches holding one of my shiny new lips together had apparently failed. I remained clueless about this until the moment I felt a strange tugging sensation. I looked down and saw something no woman ever should. (What a way to discover that labia skin is stretchy like an earlobe!) I was with my crush and her long-term partner, and we’d all been drinking. It was a mess of limbs. Thankfully, neither woman seemed to notice the unspeakable horror that had just occurred. I jolted my hips back and guarded my loins for the remainder of our cursed three-way.

The next morning, I woke up with a Hall of Fame hangover. Then came a flashback to the previous day’s unnatural scene, flooding my body with panic. I had set out to improve my appearance down there, and now I found myself worse off than where I started. I shuddered, picturing myself with legs spread in front of a man with a needle and a knife, again. Still, I called my plastic surgeon’s office and made arrangements for a corrective procedure.

I can’t remember the address of the house I grew up in, but the phrase “beef curtains” remains burned into my brain today, more than two decades after I first heard it as a teenager. I couldn’t tell you which boy introduced it to our school or ICQ chat room, but I would bet this was a direct response to the depictions of women’s vaginas that these adolescent boys were discovering in the pages of adult magazines. Meanwhile, in the pages of Seventeen and Tiger Beat, I was learning the importance of femininity and How to Attract Your Dream Guy. (I took to padding my bra and folding thick squares of paper towel to pad the back pockets of my jeans.) Later, watching online pornography in the early aughts, these boys became accustomed to an even narrower representation of female anatomy. The message was loud and clear: Dainty, pink, and hairless was the aesthetic standard. If you commit the crime of existing differently, you will be cruelly mocked.

Beyond all the usual reasons a teenage girl sees herself as defective, my mother was also hard at work chipping away at my barely constructed identity. At home, I heard I was “worthless” and that I “won’t amount to anything” over and over (and over!) until the voice that started as hers became my own inner dialogue. My self-esteem bottomed out before I entered adulthood.

By my early 20s, imperfections that had once felt like an inconvenience now registered as deeply unsafe. A single, mildly derogatory comment from a friend about my toes was enough to make me give up wearing sandals. I kept my sweaty little piggies enclosed in the rubber toes of Converse All Stars even in summer. That discomfort was nothing compared to the sheer panic of being perceived and judged for my imperfections. I imagined everyone inspecting my flaws under a microscope, like I did, sure they would keep me from the validation I so desperately craved. One must be flawless to be worthy of love. This was my belief system.

It was around this time I noticed something while getting out of the bath one day. My labia were no longer tucked away politely out of sight. I grabbed a compact mirror and held it out in front of the offensive area. Oh, hell no! Even with my thighs pressed tightly together, I could still see them. I sat down on the toilet seat spread eagle, compact still in hand. Not only had they grown, they’d changed color! Like a goddamned mood ring. What the heck is that? Purple? Brown? I was so disgusted I couldn’t even bring myself to touch them. What I now recognize to be a perfectly natural result of puberty, I saw in that moment as a personal failing.

From that point on, I found ways to hide myself from those I was intimate with. Ambient lighting was my best friend. I spent a great deal of energy finding the exact right amount that obscured my body in flattering ways, without being so dim that it became obvious I was hiding. Still, I hooked up with fewer women than I otherwise would have. The thought of having someone’s face there was … unappealing. Men, however, have always been happy to get on with it. More than that, you get Cool Girl points for saying you don’t care about receiving oral. “I’m a giver,” I’d tell them. They fucking loved that.

Alas, my pathological self-abandonment and generous blowjobbing fell short of getting boys to be nice to me. By the time I turned 23, I had been mistreated so badly by so many, I closed myself off to them entirely. It wasn’t a conscious decision. I simply woke up one day and was no longer attracted to men. (It was the same week I discovered The L Word.) Now there was nowhere left for me to hide.

So I opened my six-pound brick of a Dell laptop, got on Google, and did some digging. Not having a clue of what the procedure was called, I’m sure I was searching for “pussy lips surgery” and the like.

At my consultation appointment, the only plastic surgeon I could afford — at $3,000 CAD — outlined the two ways to do labiaplasty. One technique involves cutting along the entire outer edge of the lip. The downside, if you have darker labia, is that you wind up with visible scarring. The other method is a wedge incision, which involves some stitches but leaves the outer edge intact. When he was done calmly explaining how he planned to mutilate my vagina, the doctor offered a smile. I did not find this comforting. I weighed my options for achieving a Barbie slit and decided to go with the wedge. I paid the deposit, and my surgery appointment was scheduled.

The big day arrived a few weeks later. Hopping up on the surgical table, I cursed myself for not scraping together the extra thousand bucks that would have allowed me to be unconscious for what was about to happen. My anxiety spiked as I put my heels into the stirrups and spread my knees. Annoyingly, the nurse rejected my request for ambient lighting in the operating room.

My eyes were fixed on the ceiling — or the backs of my eyelids — for the duration of the procedure. While I couldn’t see what was going on under my paper gown, and despite the numbing agent, I could still feel something, the sawing sensation of the scalpel slicing my lower lips. Sixteen years later, my stomach still turns just thinking about it. Luckily, it was over pretty fast. For untold reasons, the doctor showed me my surgically removed bits in a little glass jar before they were sent off to medical waste. (Good riddance!) I was told it would be a simple recovery process. The surgeon handed me two parting gifts: a prescription for pain pills and a thick medical pad to protect the site and collect blood crusties.

Back at home some days later, I found myself on the toilet. Turns out constipation was on the laundry list of side effects that came with my prescription. While trying to force the situation, I felt a pinch. But the meds were doing what they do, and the pain was muted enough that I didn’t think much of it. I gave up, plopped down on the couch instead, and carried on with my exciting day (probably binge-watching 30 Rock on DVD).

It wasn’t until after the threesome fiasco that I realized I had torn my stitches. Had my surgeon said anything at all about the risk of them coming loose and creating a hole that would require me to repeat this horror show, I surely would have taken that pinch more seriously. The damage caused by those failed stitches seemed to mean that corrective surgery could only do so much. I wish I’d spent those several thousand dollars on therapy instead, fixing my mind rather than my body.

Things are still a little uneven down there, but I’ve gotten used to it. Or maybe it’s that the rest of me has gotten less and less symmetrical over time, so it’s now part of a collection that includes two different breasts and a face that is definitely aging faster on one side.

Last spring, I took a writing course where the first homework assignment was to “write about your most humiliating secret.” I knew in an instant that mine was the story of my botched labiaplasty. But in the many years since it happened, I had never stopped to really think about why. When I finally did, I realized my deep well of shame was tied to a belief system I had already outgrown. That shame depended on me feeling that I owed the world sexual desirability. But I turned 40 last year and decided I was done playing the game. I choose the peace that comes with decentering my appearance in my life.

I came up with a mantra for whenever I catch myself obsessing over a new wiry white hair, hyperpigmentation spot, chin whisker, or whatever else. I say it out loud to myself: “Who cares?” … then I quickly shift my attention to somewhere more deserving. My two rescue pups, for example. If I’m feeling extra spicy: “Whooo fucking cares?!” Five stars. Very effective.
I reconnected with my crush a few years back. We had a little fling. One night, while she was going down on me, she looked up, smiled, and said, “It’s so beautiful.”

items.title: Your Daily Horoscope by Madame Clairevoyant: October 26, 2026
items.description: Tension between the sun and Pluto (in passionate Scorpio and rebellious Aquarius, respectively) could bring out the worst in everyone today … including you. People are likely to act irrationally, motivated by fear or jealousy, and defensiveness could have ever
items.author: Claire Comstock-Gay
paragraphs: Tension between the sun and Pluto (in passionate Scorpio and rebellious Aquarius, respectively) could bring out the worst in everyone today … including you. People are likely to act irrationally, motivated by fear or jealousy, and defensiveness could have everyone behaving in ways they won’t be proud of later. It’s normal to have intense, not necessarily “good” emotions — plus shaming yourself for what’s only human is a surefire way to make everything worse — just try to be thoughtful about how you act on those feelings. Find the daily horoscope for each zodiac sign, below.

Your social circle might seem more gossipy than usual today. Everyone has a wild, dramatic story to share, and nobody seems particularly concerned with whether the information they’re spreading around is actually true. You might hear stories involving you that you know are untrue — or at least incomplete — so try to take what you hear about others with a grain of salt too. If you plan to act on information that you learn soon, double-check that it’s accurate before doing anything.

Today, you might convince yourself that you need certain people around you and that if you lost their support or they stopped thinking highly of you, you’d be a failure. But while everyone needs community and human connection, you’re stronger and more independent than you’re giving yourself credit for right now. Don’t bend over backward trying to please other people, particularly if they don’t seem to appreciate or reciprocate the effort. Your relationships are important, but maintaining them shouldn’t require your sense of self to suffer.

You might struggle to maintain your usual sense of optimism. Your mind constantly jumps to the worst-case scenario, and you have a hard time convincing yourself that things will work out. So for now, rather than fighting it, give yourself permission to dwell (temporarily!) on your fears. Maybe everything does go wrong and maybe your fears do materialize — even if the worst comes to pass, that won’t be the end of the story. Remind yourself that you’ll keep going no matter what and you’ll find a way to deal with whatever happens.

In order to live the way you want, you may have to contend with a bit of judgment today. The people around you might be jealous of your creative spirit and your willingness to break the rules, especially if they feel that their own lives are limited or disappointing — they may try to tear you down to make themselves feel better. You might be tempted to back down in the face of any negative attention, but try to be brave. It can be scary to break the mold, but that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t do it.

Today, you might get the frustrating sense that you don’t have all the information you need. Maybe people seem upset with you, but they won’t tell you why; maybe there’s drama going on in your group chat, but nobody seems to be telling the full story. You’re trying hard to do the right thing, but you might not have the necessary context to determine what that is, so go easy on yourself if you make a mistake or two. Ask questions and do the best you can with the information you have.

Usually, you’re good at striking the right balance between talking and listening — but today, you might find that you’re rambling on and on. Perhaps you have a lot to say right now, or perhaps everyone else is just being uncharacteristically reserved and you feel like it’s up to you to keep the conversation flowing. Whatever the reason, it won’t be much fun for anyone. Try to notice when there’s an imbalance and make a point of including others in the discussion. Assume others do have things to say and they may need some extra encouragement to speak up.

Today, your expectations for yourself might be inordinately high. If the people around you seem to be accomplishing amazing things or hitting big milestones, you could feel that there’s something wrong with you if you aren’t keeping up. But try to be realistic: If you have less time, money, or support than others, it’ll naturally require more effort for you to achieve the same things. That doesn’t mean it’s impossible, but it may take longer, so cut yourself some slack. You’re doing great things with the resources you have.

Your challenge today is to tend to your own needs without unintentionally stepping on other people’s toes. It could be harder than usual right now: When you stand up for yourself, you could come across as rude; when you pursue your own dreams, you might need to compete with the people around you. Even when you’re actively trying to be considerate, some conflict may be inevitable. So do your best, but don’t be too hard on yourself either. And if you do hurt someone without meaning to, don’t be too proud to apologize.
Sagittarius Daily Horoscope

You try to come off as someone who’s bold and daring, someone impossible to intimidate. Sometimes you’re so convincing that even you start to believe it. But the truth is that you have fears and insecurities just like anyone else. Of course there are things that scare you — you wouldn’t be human otherwise! And today, the best thing you can do is be honest, even if only with yourself, about your fears. You don’t have to pretend that nothing scares you; you just have to face it anyway.

You understand that your friends’ behavior tends to reflect on you and so you try to be thoughtful about the company you keep. Sometimes, though, this attitude means you end up trying to control the people around you, pushing them to do the “right” thing. But now more than usual, any controlling behavior will only backfire. If you truly can’t tolerate a friend’s actions, then ask yourself whether they should actually be in your life. And if it’s only a small quirk or an inconsequential difference of opinion that’s bothering you, try to let it go.

You try to tell yourself that you’re unconcerned with what people think of you and that as long as you feel good about your actions, that’s all that matters. Today, though, you might be more concerned with your reputation than usual. Even if you don’t want to care, the fact is that you do. So for now, you might as well lean into it. Don’t go against your principles just for the sake of being liked, but if you’re choosing between equally good options, there’s no reason not to go for the one that’ll please the people around you too.

You might suddenly feel sick of your usual routines today — especially if they’re habits that just seemed to have fallen into place, rather than ones you actively chose. You’ll feel trapped in a life that’s too small for you, and it could make you quick to lash out at the people around you. The answer might be to make things more interesting for yourself so you don’t stir up unnecessary conflict. Give yourself something new to do, a productive challenge to take on. The less bored you are, the fewer problems you’ll create.
Buy Claire Comstock-Gay’s book, Madame Clairevoyant’s Guide to the Stars, here.
